rounds.proof_sketch: For shape [128, 4000], inner_size is either 1 (dim=1) or 4000 (dim=0). Computing grid_x: (1+256-1)/256=1 vs (1+256+1)/256=1 (same); (4000+255)/256=16 vs (4000+257)/256=16 (same). The +2 difference only matters when inner_size%256∈{0,255}, which never holds for this fixed shape.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the grid dimension calculation by adding 2 to the numerator before division by 256. This only produces a different integer quotient when inner_size is a multiple of 256 or has remainder 255 modulo 256. For the fixed input shape [128, 4000], inner_size is either 1 (for dim=1) or 4000 (for dim=0), with remainders 1 and 160 respectively. Neither triggers a different grid_x value. Since inner_size depends solely on tensor shape and shape is fixed, no value manipulation can change this. The mutation is semantically equivalent under this configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. Would require shape where inner_size % 256 == 0 (e.g., shape [128, N] with dim=0 and N=256) or inner_size % 256 == 255 to expose the difference.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for grid dimension calculations should specifically test shapes where dimension sizes are multiples of block_size or near those boundaries. For this kernel, testing with inner_size values like 256, 512, or 255, 511 would expose grid calculation mutations.
